content_voiceover: This dense table converts I N R G stage into a pre-treatment risk group, and it's built from just a handful of variables, M Y C N status, age, histology or grade of differentiation, eleven-q deletion, and ploidy. The big organizing principle is that M Y C N amplification trumps almost everything else. Look across the table and notice that any stage with M Y C N amplified, whether it's L one, L two, M, or M-S, lands in the high risk group regardless of age or histology, with the sole partial exception being M-S which the slide still flags separately. For M Y C N non-amplified, stage L one alone is always very low risk. For L two, the story depends on age and eleven-q deletion, patients under eighteen months without eleven-q deletion are low risk, but adding eleven-q deletion bumps them to intermediate, and for older patients, age over five with poorly differentiated or undifferentiated histology pushes them all the way to high risk even without amplification. For stage M, M Y C N non-amplified disease in infants under eighteen months is stratified by ploidy, hyperdiploid tumors are low risk while diploid tumors are intermediate risk, reflecting that hyperdiploidy is itself a favorable biological marker in young infants. Age eighteen months or older with M stage disease, non-amplified, is high risk. Finally M-S disease under eighteen months without eleven-q deletion is very low to low risk, but M Y C N amplified M-S disease is high risk. The exam-testable takeaways are that M Y C N amplification always means high risk, hyperdiploidy is protective specifically in infants with M stage disease, and eleven-q deletion upgrades risk within L two disease.
keypoints: MYCN amplification is high risk at essentially any stage
L1, MYCN non-amplified: always very low risk
L2: age under 18mo plus no 11q deletion is low risk; 11q deletion or age over 5 with poor differentiation raises risk
M stage, MYCN non-amplified, age under 18mo: hyperdiploid is low risk, diploid is intermediate risk
MS, MYCN amplified: high risk despite otherwise favorable stage
keypoint_voiceover: MYCN amplification pushes almost any stage into the high risk group. Among MYCN non-amplified L two disease, eleven-q deletion and older age with poor differentiation both raise risk. For M stage disease in infants under eighteen months, hyperdiploidy is low risk while diploidy is intermediate risk, since ploidy is a key favorable biology marker in young infants.
